title: Target pack declaration
description: What a target pack declares, and the whole of it. specs/0004 R14 fixes the fields: identity, version, and the classes it produces with the track of each and the node types each is yielded by — and nothing else. What is deliberately absent is naming conventions, directory layout, path derivation, expansion order, and how a reference becomes a storage representation: each is stack knowledge that already lives in the pack's own agent, and declaring it would be maintenance cost with no differentiating content. specs/0012 R7 states the test — a pack declares nothing its own agent already knows AND nothing model-free needs to read. The `from` column fails the second half of that test, which is why it is here: specs/0004 R23 derives the plan with no model in the loop, so nothing else could answer which artifacts a knowledge object demands.

pack.description: The pack's identity. specs/0012 R1 records the active pack in the governed repository's own configuration, so this is the name that configuration names.

version.description: specs/0004 R30 records it in the generation manifest, so reproducing a generation names the pack version that produced it.

framework_contracts.description: specs/0012 R8: the contract versions this pack was built against, so a consumer can tell whether an installed pack and an installed framework are compatible without running them. R10 refuses a pack declaring itself against no supported version at installation rather than letting it fail during generation.

produces.description: One entry per artifact class the pack produces. specs/0004 R51 requires exactly one producer per declared class — a template on the deterministic track, a specialized agent on the judged one — so a declared class with no producer and two producers for one class are both rejected.

class.description: specs/0004 R8 closes this vocabulary and it is framework-owned. A class a pack needs and the framework does not hold is a request to change that specification, not something a pack may add.

track.description: specs/0004 R1. R2 makes the deterministic track byte-identical for identical input with no model invoked; R3 verifies the judged track against a conformance suite generated from the knowledge base. specs/0011 R2 forbids relaxing the first to keep a mechanism — a template that cannot hold byte identity moves its class here instead.

from.description: Which node types yield this class. specs/0004 R11 reports a node type yielding nothing under the active pack, which is unsatisfiable unless something can enumerate what each type yields.
